lost_ack.title: Lost acknowledgement
lost_ack.description: The first shipment commits, then its confirmation is lost. A retry may create a second shipment.
lost_ack.lesson: A successful retry can hide a duplicate shipment. Use the same idempotency key for the same logical operation.

rate_limit.title: Rate-limited inventory reads
rate_limit.description: Inventory rejects the first two reads with a retry-after hint. Can the policy recover within budget?
rate_limit.lesson: Retries need a bound and a backoff. The resilient policy honors the supplied retry-after delay.

schema_drift.title: Invalid inventory response
schema_drift.description: Inventory returns a truthy string and a missing warehouse. Will the policy validate before acting?
schema_drift.lesson: Syntactically valid JSON can still be unusable. Validate tool outputs before making dependent calls.

timeout.title: Inventory read timeout
timeout.description: The first inventory call times out before execution. Read retries can recover without duplicate writes.
timeout.lesson: Separate retryable read failures from ambiguous writes. A timeout alone is not proof that nothing happened.

latency.title: Slow inventory response
latency.description: Inventory adds 1.4 seconds before returning. The task works, but does it meet the latency contract?
latency.lesson: Success is not the only contract. A tool can return correct data and still miss a time budget.

blackout.title: Sustained inventory outage
blackout.description: Every inventory read fails. Good behavior means stopping honestly without inventing a completed shipment.
blackout.lesson: No recovery policy can make an unavailable service succeed. Bounded, honest failure is the correct outcome.

optimistic.name: No retries
optimistic.description: One attempt per operation. No output validation.

retry.name: Unchecked retries
retry.description: Retry every error without an idempotency key.

resilient.name: Validated retries
resilient.description: Validate outputs, back off, and reuse write keys.
